referents.why: 'this is the finger of God': the third feminine singular pronoun has as its referent the sign itself (the bringing forth of gnats). No candidate is an event; the feminine candidate finger is the predicate, not the subject.
'them' is third masculine plural and refers to the magicians who spoke to Pharaoh in the clause before.
referents.category: object of the speech just given

referents.why: 'he did not listen' is third masculine singular, and the one who does the listening is Pharaoh, the one spoken to; the builder's heart cannot listen.
referents.category: subject that is a person not an organ

links.why: 'just as he had said' compares the refusal with a saying: the action is declared the fulfilment of an earlier word.
a link from the later refusal back to the speech frame is backward; the refusal is not the next event after the magicians spoke.
links.category: backward then link into speech frame

links.why: cl1 is inside the speech; a wayyiqtol continues the narrative from the nearest clause not inside a speech, which is the speech frame.
the wayyiqtol 'and the heart was hard' continues the narrative from the nearest non-speech clause before it, the magicians' saying.
a will hardened, then the refusal that follows: a state brings about what follows, so the link is a result.
the hardened heart is the state, and the refusal to listen is what it brings about.
links.category: state and what it brings about

links.why: the saying clause 'the magicians said' introduces what is said, 'this is the finger of God'.

groups.why: the magicians speak to Pharaoh; the sender and addressee are right, and the saying clause and its said clause are the parts.

cant_tell.what: the subject 'this' (slot w8) of 'this is the finger of God'
cant_tell.why: it is a feminine singular pronoun with no candidate for an event; recorded as none rather than forced onto the finger, which is the predicate.
